design_condition: The building completes the existing L-shaped facility and closes the schoolyard toward the open space, but separates the sports fields from the school complex and narrows the access route.

positive.statement: The building is precisely fitted into its surroundings and closes the schoolyard from the open space.
Its structure takes up the proportions of the existing classroom wing.
The access axis is extended and improves access to the entire facility.
The basic levels meet the requirements of their school level ideally, with autonomous and well-thought-out room units.
The spacious terrace allows the interior space to expand in uncertain weather.
The day school is well organized.
The primary classes and design rooms are separately accessible, with convenient underground access for frequent class changes.
The planned building envelope can easily achieve the required energy standard.

negative.statement: The sports fields are separated from the school complex and can only be reached by indirect routes.
The access from the main path seems too narrow.
The arrangement is attractive for the ground-floor classes, but its potential is not exhausted for the day school.
The day school would be better placed on the ground floor, and the proposed outside stair may not solve the operational problem.
The upper-floor primary-school areas lack a connection to the schoolyard or a view outside.
The facade appears rough and almost foreign beside the existing building.
The incorporation of the energy concept into the project is largely missing.
The project remains undecided in many places and lacks an underlying idea that holds it together.
